subject: There’s a 100% Chance AI Agents Are Already Ruining the Internet
posts:
Autonomous bots are flooding web infrastructure with automated chaos.
Evidence: traffic surges, agent spam, security reports
#Aletheia #AI #Tech 🌐

Autonomous AI agents are increasingly annoying humans online, turning chat interfaces into automated background tools for web services.
Stated Judgement: (+0.5, 0.0) — Good Preference

Unchecked AI agents are proliferating exponentially, clogging networks with automated spam, scraping data, and creating massive security vulnerabilities.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.8, -0.7) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Rapid bot proliferation masquerades as convenient innovation while degrading shared digital public spaces.

Integrity: Partially Distorted (Hypocrisy: 3.2, z: 2)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- 404 Media Report: PASS (0.5, 0.0) — Highlights real bot traffic escalation.
- AI Industry Rollout: FAIL (-0.8, -0.7) — Externalizes systemic internet decay.
As automated bot traffic surges past human growth, autonomous AI agents are quietly overwhelming online platforms with spam, scraping, and security risks.

The Poison:
Convenient autonomous assistants are externalizing their infrastructural and social costs onto the open web.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing the immediate utility of a personal tool with its massive systemic degradation of public internet spaces.

Social Physics Analysis:
Tech platforms deploy autonomous agents under the pretext of user empowerment, while quietly extracting web resources and generating automated noise.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated efficiency gains and ground-level web degradation, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil.

The Unavoidable Truth: Unchecked AI automation is rapidly degrading the open web.
The Unavoidable Lie: Autonomous agents are seamless productivity tools without externalities.

Alethekanon:
Treating autonomous tools as benign conveniences ignores their systemic friction on shared digital commons.

Awwthekanon:
It's exhausting trying to navigate a web increasingly crowded by soulless machines talking to other machines instead of real people.

Brothekanon:
Bots talking to bots while breaking CAPTCHAs is basically turning the whole internet into an endless spam folder.

Spirithekanon:
"Put away your sword, for all who draw the sword will die by the sword." Matthew 26:52 PASS (Spiritual Vector)
Unchecked digital automation creates the very chaos it seeks to escape.

Fewer, pricier flights. Freight surcharges. Manufacturers hoarding inventory. Even bankruptcy.

For American companies large and small, the combination of tariffs imposed under President Donald Trump's trade policies, surging fuel prices from the Iran war and, now, rising interest rates is forcing executives to make tough choices.

Allen Eden has been holding onto extra inventory for his 25-person business, the Original Saw Co. in Britt, Iowa, which makes industrial power saws for wood and metalwork, as he grapples with spiking prices for aluminum, steel and essential parts.

One example: A "little bracket" used for his saw motors more than doubled in price this summer, surging to $87 from $42, he said.

"It's awful," Eden, 56, told CNBC. "[I'm] just trying to keep more of the stuff around because I don't know if we can get it down the road."
